recentItems.title: Adidas faces boycott calls over campaign featuring former Israeli soldier
recentItems.description:
Sportswear giant Adidas is facing criticism after a former Israeli soldier appeared in a local campaign promoting its single-shoe service for amputees. Shalev Biton lost his leg after being wounded during the 2021 Israel-Gaza conflict. The World Health Organization estimates that more than 5,000 traumatic limb amputations have taken place in Gaza since October 2023. Stephanie Westbrook, a sports boycotts campaigns coordinator for PACBI and a founding member of the BDS movement, told Al Jazeera the campaign is "an absolute affront to the Palestinians." She said: "Gaza now has the highest number of child amputees per capita anywhere in the world," and accused Israel of imposing a "medieval siege" that is preventing prosthetics from entering Gaza. Westbrook said the controversy is "dangerous" because, in her view, it normalises Israel's actions against Palestinians and allows what she describes as crimes to continue "with impunity."

recentItems.title: Bolivia army base blast leaves families desperate for news of missing soldiers
recentItems.description:
The death toll from an explosion at an army base in the Bolivian city of Viacha has risen to three after rescuers recovered another body from the wreckage. Fourteen people remain missing, most of them young conscripts aged 18 or 19 who were serving their first year of national service. The blast destroyed a building at an artillery regiment, damaged nearby structures and injured more than 80 people. Officials say a stockpile of fireworks exploded, but the exact cause remains under investigation. Firefighters are continuing to search the debris for those still missing, while anxious families have gathered outside the site demanding information about their loved ones. Some relatives say missing soldiers were assigned to other duties and question why they were at the building when the explosion happened. Bolivia's President Rodrigo Paz has promised a transparent investigation as authorities work to establish what caused the blast and whether proper safety protocols were followed. 

Al Jazeera's Ferdia Carr reports.

recentItems.title: US and Iran traded attacks on warships and tankers amid Strait of Hormuz tensions on Saturday
recentItems.description:
On Saturday, the US military struck and destroyed three Iranian crude oil tankers near Kharg Island and in the Gulf of Oman, after Iran fired ballistic missiles at two US warships — an aircraft carrier and a guided-missile destroyer. Central Command says the US ships successfully evaded the attacks and no US personnel were harmed, while two of the Iranian vessels were disabled and the third completely destroyed. US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said: "It's simple. If Iran shoots at US ships, we will destroy and sink their oil tankers." Iran's Foreign Ministry strongly condemned the US "acts of aggression", while the IRGC claimed it responded by targeting three oil tankers travelling through an "unauthorised" route in the Strait of Hormuz and three US-affiliated vessels. There has been no independent confirmation of the Iranian claims. The tit-for-tat attacks mark a significant escalation between Washington and Tehran. 

Al Jazeera's Manuel Rapalo reports from Washington, DC.

recentItems.title: Yemen fighting intensifies as government forces counterattack Houthis
recentItems.description:
Fighting has intensified in western Yemen as government-aligned forces launch counterattacks against the Iran-backed Houthi rebels, officially known as Ansar Allah, around Hodeidah and Taiz. Dozens of people, including civilians, were reported killed on Saturday as the Houthis pushed across several fronts before government forces sent reinforcements and launched their own air strikes. The fighting has also forced families to flee their homes around Maqbanah and Jabal Habashi, with some arriving at displacement camps with few belongings. Yemen has remained divided since the Houthis seized the capital, Sanaa, in 2014 and expanded their control across much of the north and west. A truce in 2022 reduced violence but failed to produce a lasting peace. The latest fighting is centred on a strategically important corridor leading towards the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, a major global shipping route connecting the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden. With both sides reinforcing their positions, fears are growing that the renewed offensive could trigger a wider escalation. 

Al Jazeera's Aksel Zaimovic reports.
